label: Secretory_Carcinoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Secretory carcinoma exhibits ETV6 rearrangement, often involving ETV6::NTRK3 [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).
- Commonly seen in elder males, presenting as a unilocular mass.
- Histologically characterized by microcystic, tubular, and solid structures with eosinophilic secretions.
- Positive for S100; negative for DOG1, p63, and p40 [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html).
- Differential diagnosis includes acinic cell carcinoma and low-grade mucoepidermoid carcinoma.

## Terminology
- **Secretory carcinoma**: A salivary gland–type carcinoma with microcystic, tubular, and solid architectures.
- Formerly known as "mammary analogue secretory carcinoma" (not recommended).

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - ETV6 rearrangement, frequently ETV6::NTRK3 [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).
  - Microcystic, tubular, and solid growth patterns with eosinophilic secretions [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).
- **Desirable:**
  - Abundant eosinophilic homogeneous or bubbly secretions.
  - Immunohistochemical positivity for S100 and negative p63/p40/DOG1 [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html).

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- Driven by ETV6 rearrangements, particularly ETV6::NTRK3 translocation [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).

## Clinical Issues
  - **Epidemiology**: Elder males, peak in the seventh decade [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html).
  - **Site**: Frequently occurs in major salivary glands.
  - **Presentation**: Typically presents as a uninodular mass.
  - **Prognosis**: Relatively favorable with appropriate treatment.

## Microscopic
- Predominantly microcystic, tubular, and solid architectural patterns.
  - Abundant eosinophilic or bubbly secretions.
- Cells with mild to moderate nuclear atypia and occasional multinucleation.

## Ancillary Tests
- **Immunohistochemistry:**
  - S100: Positive.
  - MUC4: Positive.
  - p63, p40, DOG1: Negative [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html).
- **Molecular/genetics:**
  - ETV6::NTRK3 fusion [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Secretory_Carcinoma.html).

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Acinic Cell Carcinoma:**
  - Negative p63/p40/DOG1 for secretory carcinoma vs acinic cell carcinoma [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsmalignant.html).
  - Acinic cell typically has granular cytoplasm with zymogen granules.

- **Low-Grade Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma:**
  - Presence of mucous and epidermoid cells.
  - Lacks ETV6 rearrangement.

- **Salivary Duct Carcinoma Variants**:
  - More aggressive, often with apocrine differentiation.
  - AR and HER2 positivity [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandssalivaryductcarcinoma.html).

- **Myoepithelial Carcinoma Variants**:
  - Shows myoepithelial markers like SMA, calponin [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsepimyocarcinoma.html).

- **Mucinous Adenocarcinoma** ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Mucinous_Adenocarcinoma.html)):
  - Excludes other mucin-producing carcinomas. 
  - Differentiated by histological pattern and molecular profile.

cards.title: Mucinous adenocarcinoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Mucinous adenocarcinoma Section: differential_diagnosis To diagnose MA, other mucin-producing salivary gland carcinomas must be excluded, including mucin-rich mucoepidermoid carcinoma (epidermoid/intermediate cells; p63/p40+), mucinous and rhabdoid variants of salivary duct carcinoma (apocrine cytology; AR+), and the mucinous/secretory pattern of myoepithelial carcinoma (nested/corded pattern; S100, calponin, or SMA+). Metastasis from gastrointestinal, pancreaticobiliary, or lung adenocarcinomas should be ruled out clinically.

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Secretory carcinoma Section: clinical SC usually presents as a uninodular mass. Compression or invasion of adjacent structures and nodal disease are more common than in salivary SC. --- Average age at presentation is slightly older than at salivary gland sites (61.5 years, range: 36–74 years). There appears to be a female predilection.

cards.excerpt: Entity: Secretory carcinoma Section: definition Secretory carcinoma (SC) is a salivary gland–type carcinoma often composed of microcystic, tubular, and solid structures with abundant eosinophilic homogeneous or bubbly secretions. It is usually characterized by specific rearrangement of the ETV6 gene.

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Essential features
cards.heading: Essential features
cards.text_excerpt:
Rare primary salivary gland carcinoma characterized by ETV6 gene rearrangement (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599, Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295, Am J Surg Pathol 2018;42:1121)
Predominantly (76%) occurs in parotid, minor salivary glands of oral cavity and submandibular gland
Also described in nasal cavity, skin and thyroid (Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295)
Predominantly adults, wide age range (5 - 87 years) (Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295, Histopathology 2012;61:387)
Various histological growth patterns, including cystic, solid, tubular, papillary cystic and lobular
Cysts with intraluminal colloid-like secretions (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599)
Cells with bubbly cytoplasm and relatively monotonous round nuclei with small but distinct nucleoli (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599, Histopathology 2012;61:387, Pathology 2015;47:659)
Immunohistochemical expression of GATA3, S100, NTRK3, MUC4, mammaglobin (Pathology 2015;47:659, Head Neck Pathol 2013;7:311, Histopathology 2020;76:375)
Generally low grade with indolent clinical behavior; however, local lymph node metastases may be seen in up to 22% (Histopathology 2012;61:387)
Rare high grade transformation with aggressive clinical behavior, including distant metastasis (Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112, Int J Surg Pathol 2017;25:613, Ann Oncol 2016;27:920)

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Clinical features
cards.heading: Clinical features
cards.text_excerpt:
Slow growing painless mass; mean duration: 1 year (Head Neck 2019;41:1227, Oral Oncol 2018;82:29)
Low T stage at diagnosis (almost always T1 or T2) (Oral Oncol 2018;82:29, Pathology 2015;47:659)
Generally indolent clinical course with recurrence rates of < 10% and 10 year overall survival of 95% after macroscopically complete resection (Head Neck 2019;41:1227)
Local lymph node involvement at diagnosis in a minority (5 - 22%) (JAMA Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2019;145:91, Histopathology 2012;61:387)
Distant metastases in < 5% (JAMA Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2019;145:91, Head Neck 2019;41:1227)
Locally aggressive behavior and poor outcomes have been reported if incompletely resected (Head Neck 2019;41:1227, Pathology 2015;47:659)
High grade transformation with aggressive clinical behavior including distant metastasis has been reported (Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112, Int J Surg Pathol 2017;25:613)

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Prognostic factors
cards.heading: Prognostic factors
cards.text_excerpt:
pT stage of 3 or 4 and high grade features appear most strongly associated with poor clinical outcomes (Head Neck 2019;41:1227, Pathology 2015;47:659)
While definite thresholds are not yet described, nuclear pleomorphism, easily identified mitotic activity or presence of comedonecrosis have been described to confer poor prognosis (Int J Clin Exp Pathol 2014;7:9008)
Rare high grade transformation with aggressive clinical behavior including distant metastasis has been reported (Am J Surg Pathol 2014;38:23, Am J Surg Pathol 2018;42:1121, Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112, Int J Surg Pathol 2017;25:613)

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Treatment
cards.heading: Treatment
cards.text_excerpt:
Primary resection
Neck dissection or adjuvant radiotherapy if adverse prognostic features or evidence of lymph node metastases present (JAMA Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2019;145:91, Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112, Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2021;164:27)
TRK inhibitors have shown promise in phase 1 and 2 trials for ETV6-NTRK3 rearranged tumors but efficacy is not established (N Engl J Med 2018;378:731)
Cases of initial response followed by acquired resistance have been reported in advanced disease (Ann Oncol 2016;27:920, Int J Surg Pathol 2017;25:613)

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Circumscribed or infiltrative edge
cards.heading: Circumscribed or infiltrative edge
cards.text_excerpt:
Lobulated architecture
Variable arrangements, including macrocystic, microcystic, solid, tubular, follicular and papillary cystic patterns (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599, Am J Surg Pathol 2019;43:1483)
Pale eosinophilic colloid-like intraluminal secretions; secretions are periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) reagent positive and diastase resistant (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599)
Tumor cells have eosinophilic or vacuolated cytoplasm and monomorphic round vesicular nuclei with small but distinctive nucleoli
Occasional lymphovascular invasion and perineural invasion are seen (Head Neck 2019;41:1227)
High grade transformation has been reported with a distinct population of tumor cells exhibiting solid or trabecular growth, infiltrative margins, desmoplastic stromal reaction, comedo-like necrosis, nuclear pleomorphism, increased mitotic rate, loss of secretory activity and perineural invasion
A distinct low grade (conventional) carcinomatous component is also present (Pathol Res Pract 2017;213:1112)
Microscopic (histologic) imagesContributed by Ruta Gupta, M.B.B.S., M.D.

S100: 100% sensitive, 67% specific when compared with acinic cell carcinoma (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599)
SOX10: 100% sensitive (Hum Pathol 2016;56:134)
Not specific, as a variety of salivary gland tumors including acinic cell carcinoma can show staining
MUC4: 91% sensitivity, 100% specificity (Histopathology 2020 Sep 15 [Epub ahead of print])

cards.title: Secretory carcinoma — Molecular / cytogenetics description
cards.heading: Molecular / cytogenetics description
cards.text_excerpt:
Recurrent translocation t(12;15)(p13;q24), resulting in fusion of ETV6 on chromosome 12 and NTRK3 on chromosome 15 (Am J Surg Pathol 2010;34:599)
Alternate fusion partners have been identified, including ETV6-RET and ETV6-MET (Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295, Hum Pathol 2019;83:50, Am J Surg Pathol 2018;42:1121)
Potential role of other non-ETV6 translocations according to recent reports: VIM-RET and CTNNA1-ALK (Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:1295, Am J Surg Pathol 2020;44:962)
